# R3 — Rubix Ranked RAG

> Provenance-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation system for mailbox and
> document knowledge bases. Every answer is grounded in ranked, cited
> chunks (vector similarity + keyword overlap + recency) and every
> citation traces back to a specific source_id/load_id/timestamp — no
> answer is generated without retrieval, and no source is ever fabricated.

R3 is a single Go binary with an embedded vector store (tinySQL or
SQLite) and an embedded browser frontend — no separate database or build
step. It imports PST mailbox exports (incl. attachments), plain
files/Office/PDF documents, SharePoint, Exchange Online/IMAP mail (incl.
attachments), Microsoft Teams channels, Confluence pages, Jira issues and
generic websites, then answers questions with inline `[Qn]` citation
markers resolved against the sources that actually grounded the answer.
Every connector is read-only against its source system, with one
deliberate, human-in-the-loop exception: draft-reply generation
(`draft.go`) can *append* a proposed reply to a mailbox's Drafts folder
for a person to review/edit/discard — R3 never sends mail autonomously,
and nothing else in this codebase writes to a connected system at all.

## For LLM agents calling this instance

- `POST /api/ask` — ask a question, get a cited answer. Body:
  `{"question": "...", "format": "json"}` for a single buffered
  `{"answer": "...", "citations": [...]}` response (recommended for
  non-browser callers), or omit `format` for an NDJSON token stream. See
  `/api/openapi.json` for the full request/response schema.
- `POST /api/search` — ranked retrieval only, no LLM call: returns the
  scored chunks a question would be grounded in, without generating an
  answer. Useful for a caller that wants to do its own answer synthesis.
- `GET /api/openapi.json` — machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0 spec for both
  endpoints above; load this into any codegen/agent tool instead of
  hand-parsing this file.
- Auth: open by default; if `settings.api.require_api_key` is enabled,
  send `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A missing/
  invalid key on a gated instance returns `401`.
- `GET /healthz` — liveness probe, no auth, no dependency checks.
- Also reachable via MCP (`r3_ask`/`r3_search` tools) for MCP-speaking
  agents (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, etc.), and via a small `r3cli`
  wrapper for terminal/scripting use — see `docs/API.md` for both.

## Docs (in this repository, not served by the running instance)

- `README.md` — architecture, data sources, configuration, security
  posture; the canonical technical reference (English).
- `ANLEITUNG.md` — the same ground covered operationally, in German, for
  day-to-day running/configuring/extending R3.
- `AGENTS.md` — environment-specific notes for AI coding agents working
  on this codebase (toolchain quirks, build scope, etc.), not relevant to
  an agent only *calling* the running API above.

## Notes for agents answering questions about R3 itself

- Every citation an answer returns already passed two filters server-side
  (see README.md "Security / privacy considerations"): it was actually
  referenced by the model (not just retrieved), and its source_kind isn't
  configured as hidden (`source_visibility`) or department-restricted
  (`source_access`) for the requester. Don't assume a citation list you
  receive is the complete set of everything that *could* have been
  retrieved — restricted/unused candidates are dropped before you see them.
- R3 has no built-in authentication beyond the optional API key above and
  optional LDAP-gated admin routes — treat any instance you're pointed at
  as potentially open to whoever can reach it on the network, and don't
  assume every deployment restricts access the same way.
